name: Sweet Potato
description: A warm-season vine producing nutritious, sweet orange tubers. Grown from slips (rooted cuttings) rather than seeds. Excellent source of vitamins A and C.
tips: Purchase certified disease-free slips from reputable suppliers. Hill soil around plants as they grow. Harvest before first frost for best storage.
yield: 3-6 pounds per plant, depending on variety and growing conditions.

soil.notes: Avoid heavy clay or waterlogged soils. Excessive nitrogen produces lush vines but small tubers.

temperature.notes: Requires long, warm growing season. Very sensitive to cold and frost damage.

environmentalAlerts.message: Harvest immediately - sweet potatoes are damaged by temperatures below 50°F.
Reduce watering near harvest to prevent tuber cracking and storage issues.

storage.method: Cure then store in cool, dry place
storage.notes: Cure in warm, humid conditions for 7-10 days, then store at 55-60°F with high humidity.

careTasks.name: Plant slips
careTasks.description: Plant rooted slips when soil temperature reaches 60°F and all danger of frost has passed.

careTasks.name: Hill soil
careTasks.description: Mound soil around the base of plants to encourage tuber formation and prevent greening.

careTasks.name: Side-dress with fertilizer
careTasks.description: Apply low-nitrogen fertilizer to encourage tuber development rather than excessive vine growth.

careTasks.name: Harvest tubers
careTasks.description: Harvest before first frost. Dig carefully to avoid bruising. Brush off soil but don't wash.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water regularly early in season, then reduce as harvest approaches. Avoid overhead watering.

name: Parsnip
description: A long-season root vegetable with cream-colored, carrot-shaped roots and sweet, nutty flavor that improves after frost. Related to carrots but more cold-hardy.
tips: Seeds have poor germination - sow thickly and thin later. Can remain in ground through winter in most climates for sweetest flavor.
succession: Not recommended - long growing season makes succession planting impractical.
yield: 1 root per plant, typically 8-12 inches long.

soil.type: Deep, loose, well-drained soil free of stones and debris.
soil.notes: Deep soil preparation essential for straight, long roots. Avoid fresh manure which causes forked roots.

temperature.notes: Cool-season crop that tolerates hard frost. Flavor improves significantly after exposure to cold weather.

environmentalAlerts.message: Mulch heavily to keep soil cool during summer heat to prevent poor root development.

storage.method: Leave in ground or store in root cellar
storage.duration: All winter in ground, 4-6 months in storage
storage.notes: Best left in ground and harvested as needed. Store harvested roots in damp sand at 32-35°F.

careTasks.name: Direct sowing
careTasks.description: Sow fresh seeds directly in prepared bed. Seeds lose viability quickly and germination is slow.

careTasks.name: Thin seedlings
careTasks.description: Thin crowded seedlings to final spacing when 2 inches tall. Handle gently to avoid root damage.

careTasks.name: Mulch heavily
careTasks.description: Apply thick mulch to suppress weeds and keep soil consistently moist and cool.

careTasks.name: Begin harvest
careTasks.description: Begin harvesting after first frost for sweetest flavor. Roots can remain in ground all winter.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Water consistently to prevent cracking. Deep, infrequent watering encourages straight root development.
